latest.title: Welsh hospitals extend routine MT-RNR1 testing
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 1358U

10 September 2026
10 September 2026
​
genedrive plc
("genedrive" or the "Company")
Welsh hospitals extend routine clinical service of genedrive's MT-RNR1 test
-
Seven of the 14 UK sites participating in the PALOH-UK Programme now in routine clinical service demonstrating growing adoption of Genedrive® MT-RNR1 in NHS neonatal care
-
PALOH-UK patient recruitment has now completed with nearly 6,000 babies tested
genedrive plc (AIM: GDR), the point of care pharmacogenetic testing company, is pleased to announce that Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board and Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, will extend routine clinical service of the Genedrive® MT-RNR1 ID kit for the prevention of Antibiotic Induced Hearing Loss ("AIHL") in neonates admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Units ("NICU"). Continuation is funded, effective from 1 May 2026, until the outcome of the final NICE assessment expected in July 2027.
These hospitals together represent approximately 750 NICU admissions annually and are two of the 14 sites participating in the PALOH-UK programme, which was established to address National Institute for Clinical Care and Excellence ("NICE") Real World Evidence generation requirements. Since the introduction of the test in the UK, more than 40 critically ill babies have been identified with the MT-RNR1 variant, allowing clinicians to prescribe an alternative antibiotic and helping to prevent AIHL.
The extension of routine clinical service in Wales follows recent business-as-usual adoption at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust and University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust, demonstrating continued progress in genedrive's ambition to transition the MT-RNR1 test from evidence generation into routine NHS clinical practice.
Dr Gino Miele, CEO of genedrive plc, said:
"We are delighted that these hospitals in Wales have extended the routine clinical use of our rapid MT-RNR1 genetic test through to the expected issuance of final guidance by NICE. This commitment ensures babies and families in Wales will continue to benefit from timely access to this preventive genetic test and demonstrates the important role NHS Wales is playing in integrating rapid pharmacogenetic testing into routine neonatal care.
"Seven of the 14 sites participating in the PALOH-UK programme have now transitioned to routine clinical use of our MT-RNR1 test. We are in active discussions with the remaining hospitals, helping to ensure that newborn babies across the UK continue to have access to this preventive test."
Patient recruitment in the PALOH-UK programme has been completed, with nearly 6,000 babies in neonatal care receiving the Genedrive® MT-RNR1 ID test. Clinical cohort analysis is underway with publication expected in scientific literature around October 2026. Funding for PALOH-UK sites is provided by the Office for Life Sciences ("OLS") and National Institute for Health and Care Research ("NIHR").
Following completion of patient recruitment, the Genedrive® MT-RNR1 ID Kit has exited NICE's Early Value Assessment pathway and has been selected for technology appraisal following ministerial referral from the Department of Health and Social Care. The test currently has a conditional NICE recommendation. NHS England has communicated an anticipated tender notice publication date of 1 January 2027 and a go-live target of July 2027, subject to the outcome of NICE guidance.

Headquartered in Manchester, genedrive is focused on scaling UK-developed precision diagnostics within routine care and leveraging real-world evidence to support broader international adoption and commercial growth.

Board Appointments
genedrive plc (AIM: GDR), the point of care pharmacogenetic testing company, today announces that Mr Mark Winkler and Mr Mike Fairbourn have agreed to join the Board as independent Non-Executive Directors with effect from 1 September 2026.
The appointments strengthen the Board's financial, strategic, healthcare and commercial expertise as genedrive enters its next phase of growth, focused on scaling adoption of its pharmacogenetic tests in the UK and expanding its international business.
Mark brings extensive financial, strategic and corporate finance experience, advising growth companies, multinational businesses and investors on strategy, finance, governance and growth capital. He is the founder and CEO of Red Earth Advisors and previously held senior roles at Stonehage Fleming and Deloitte where he qualified as an ACA.
Mike brings more than three decades of commercial and leadership experience across the pharmaceutical and medical technology sectors. He spent almost 20 years at global medical technology company Becton Dickinson, including as Vice President and General Manager for the UK and Ireland, and served for ten years on the Board of the Association of British HealthTech Industries ("ABHI"), the UK's leading industry association for health technology, including products such as single use devices, diagnostics and digitally enhanced technologies.
It is proposed that Mark Winkler will chair the Company's Audit and Remuneration Committees.
As previously communicated, Chris Yates, who has served on the Board since 2018, has today stepped down as a Non-Executive Director in order to focus on his other professional commitments.
Mr Graham Cole CBE, Chairman of genedrive plc, said:
"Mark and Mike bring highly complementary experience and skills to the Board at an important stage for genedrive as we build on the progress already made and look to further scale the business. Their experience will be invaluable as we focus on broadening adoption of our pharmacogenetic tests, strengthening commercial execution and delivering sustainable growth and value for shareholders.
"
On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Chris for his commitment and significant contribution to genedrive over the past eight years, and for his support during this period of Board transition. We wish him continued success in the future."
Mr Mark Winkler, Non-Executive Director of genedrive plc, said:
"genedrive has built a strong foundation and I look forward to working with Graham, Gino and the wider Board, bringing my financial, strategic and governance experience to support disciplined growth and the Company's ambitions as it scales."
Mr Mike Fairbourn, Non-Executive Director of genedrive plc, said:
"
genedrive has developed innovative pharmacogenetic tests addressing important clinical needs. Having spent much of my career working at the interface between healthcare innovation and clinical practice, I am particularly excited by the opportunity to help broaden adoption and embed these technologies into healthcare pathways in the UK and internationally."

company_30s.what_they_do: Genedrive makes handheld, rapid genetic tests that let doctors diagnose bacterial infections and antibiotic resistance right at the patient’s bedside, cutting the time from sample to result from days to minutes.
company_30s.why_they_matter: With antibiotic resistance rising, fast, accurate diagnostics are a critical tool for better patient care and for curbing unnecessary antibiotic use. Genedrive’s tests fill a niche that hospitals, labs and community clinics need, and the market for rapid point‑of‑care diagnostics is projected to grow into the billions.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in a growth phase, expanding its product line, securing regulatory approvals and building NHS and commercial partnerships. It’s trading at a very low price, reflecting its pre‑profit status and the high uncertainty around how quickly it will capture market share.

rns_narrative: Regulatory momentum: The company has just received NHS guideline endorsement for its MT‑RNR1 test and several CE‑IVD approvals across Europe, signalling that the tests are ready for clinical rollout.

Partnership and funding: A new deal with Thermo Fisher Scientific for distribution and a £3 million grant from Southampton University to develop safer medicines for older patients suggest external validation and fresh capital.
Clinical adoption: Multiple NHS trusts have already started using the test as part of routine care, and the company is moving from pilot to full‑scale implementation in the UK.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – the chatter is sparse but focused on upcoming NHS roll‑out.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls highlight the strategic partnership with Thermo Fisher and the rapid NHS adoption as evidence that Genedrive is on track to become a key player in antibiotic stewardship.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the limited current revenue, heavy cash burn, and fierce competition from larger diagnostics firms that could crowd out Genedrive’s market share.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The conversation has shifted from skeptical “can it scale?” to hopeful “will the NHS adopt it widely?” – a subtle but positive turn.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no public interest spikes, which is a green flag for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: Official NHS rollout announcement for the MT‑RNR1 test – a clear sign that the market has accepted the product.
Thermo Fisher distribution launch – will bring Genedrive to a global customer base.
Positive results from the UK clinical guideline implementation – could unlock additional funding and reimbursement.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that breaks the recent low, a price breakout above the 200‑day moving average, or a news bulletin announcing a new partnership or regulatory approval.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a deep capitulation. The APEX score is high enough that a sharp mean‑reversion bounce is plausible once a catalyst confirms adoption.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The signal color is GREEN – a 70‑85% crash – and the company is now lining up the two biggest catalysts: NHS adoption and a Thermo Fisher deal. If the stock recovers to the halfway point of its crash, the upside is roughly 100‑150% with a single trade. The historical GREEN average return of 39% and win‑rate of 40% show that deep crashes often end up big.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the NHS rollout stalls, or if a competitor launches a cheaper, faster test, the price could stay near its current low. The firm’s cash burn and lack of current revenue also mean it could struggle to sustain operations if adoption is slow.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped at the current price (near zero). Potential gain is 2–3 times that if the stock rebounds to the mid‑crash level. The asymmetry is therefore highly favorable for a contrarian long.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback that confirms the 200‑day SMA, size 5–10% of your discretionary account, and set a stop just below the recent low. Use a trailing stop to lock in gains as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a clear NHS announcement or a Thermo Fisher distribution launch. A volume spike of 30% above the 20‑day average is a good trigger.
playbook.if_passing: No terminal risk identified; the only risk is a failure to roll out the test. If that occurs, consider cutting the position.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Deep crash, imminent NHS adoption and a Thermo Fisher partnership create a high‑reward, low‑downside contrarian opportunity for GDR.L.
